title: Esther
lead: Esther, also called Hadassah, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa, became queen of the Persian king Ahasuerus and risked her life to save her people from Haman's decree. The book named for her is one of the five Megillot, read at Purim.

sections.h: Esther in the Bible and after
sections.b: Esther appears only in the book that bears her name. An orphan of the tribe of Benjamin, daughter of Abihail and cousin of Mordecai (Esther 2:7, 15), she is taken into the king's house, keeps her people a secret at Mordecai's command (Esther 2:10, 20), and is made queen (Esther 2:17). When Haman's decree threatens the Jews, she hesitates, then fasts and goes to the king unasked: "And if I perish, I perish" (Esther 4:16). Through two feasts she exposes Haman (Esther 5–7), wins a counter-decree (Esther 8) and, with Mordecai, writes to confirm Purim (Esther 9:29–32). The Greek Esther adds her prayer and her fainting approach to the king (Additions C and D). The rabbis count her among the seven prophetesses (Bavli Megillah 14a), and Christians long read her as a model of courage and of intercession.
